verdicts.evidence: Own run (deltat_ae.mjs + deltat_cmp.py): astronomy-engine 2.1.19 MakeTime gives TT-UT = 75.50 s at 2026-09-22T17:00Z, Swiss deltat_ex(FLG_SWIEPH) 68.82 s, difference +6.68 s; +2.75 s at 2020-12-21, +11.95 s at 2038-01-19, +27.86 s at 2055-06-06, all matching the claim. Independent ground truth fetched from IERS finals2000A.daily (USNO mirror; datacenter.iers.org reset the connection): UT1-UTC = -0.0114 s at MJD 61305 (2026-09-22, flag I = observed), so the true Delta-T is 32.184+37+0.0114 = 69.195 s: astronomy-engine is +6.30 s wrong, Swiss -0.37 s, and the Horizons clock implied from the cached Moon_UT vs Moon requests (horizons_dt.py: +0.364 s vs Swiss at D4) is 69.18 s, within 0.01 s of IERS. astronomy-engine already sits outside the observed band [68.28,70.08] from about 2018 (71.85 s at 2020-07-01). Moon rate at the instant is 12.31 deg/day = 0.513 arcsec/s, so 6.3 s is 3.2 arcsec; the shipped engine's c_raw Moon at D4 is +3.64 arcsec from Swiss (auditor: 3.505 vs Horizons UT), consistent. Code path verified: node_modules/@zodiacs/engine/dist/chunk-GBH7JIYF.js imports MakeTime from astronomy-engine (line 20); astronomy-engine esm/astronomy.js:1131 `let DeltaT = DeltaT_EspenakMeeus`. Note for the fix: astronomy-engine exports SetDeltaTFunction (astronomy.js:1132), so an IERS-table Delta-T can be injected without forking. The receipt CONVENTIONS declare no Delta-T model and the public methodology page attributes Delta-T disagreement only to far-future extrapolation (2100), so the present-day error is undocumented. Major is earned: a current-epoch accuracy gap that keeps the production Moon below Swiss and below Swiss's Moshier fallback; not blocking because no documented guarantee is falsified.

Independent rerun with Swiss as the instrument rather than Horizons (swiss_corpus.py, engine_corpus.mjs, compare_corpus.py over the auditor's 24 preregistered instants; every SWIEPH call returned retflag 258 and every Moshier call 260, checked): @zodiacs/engine 0.1.1-rc.6 with its clock pinned to Swiss Delta-T is max 18.85 arcsec / p50 2.07 arcsec in longitude from Swiss .se1 (per body max: Neptune 18.85, Pluto 14.31, Venus 12.64, Uranus 12.07, Saturn 10.27, Mercury 7.97, Jupiter 7.74, Mars 4.41, Moon 3.88, Sun 1.35) and max 19.03 arcsec in latitude (Saturn, p50 8.19; Uranus 16.42; Neptune 9.71). Swiss with no data files (set_ephe_path to a nonexistent dir, FLG_MOSEPH, retflag 260) is max 2.82 arcsec (Pluto), Neptune 2.05, Moon 1.25, Sun 0.066 from the .se1 answer. All numbers within the claim. The ratio of overall maxima is 6.7x (inside the stated 4-10x); per body it runs from 3x (Moon) to over 100x (Mercury), so the headline understates for inner bodies. Cause check: the Saturn latitude residual is +4.4 arcsec at C1 and +17.6 at C4 with Saturn at nearly the same longitude (249.9 vs 249.7 deg), so it is not an ecliptic-frame tilt; consistent with truncated VSOP87 latitude series as the auditor states. Severity: major, not blocking; src/pages/methodology/index.astro:88-90 and developers/engine/index.astro:162-163 already publish 'worst 18.6 arcsec vs Swiss', so no documented claim is falsified, but the gap versus every Swiss configuration including zero-data Moshier is real.

Facts confirmed: sha256 sepl_18.se1 = ca1393ceab3a44fb..., semo_18.se1 = 1ca07bd67c24374d..., matching docs/platform/evidence/swiss-benchmark/CONFIGURATION.md line 14; both file headers read 'Created for Astrodienst in Switzerland 2026/05/26, based on JPL Ephemeris DE441.'; RESULTS.md line 231 says 'Swiss's semo_18.se1 is a fit to DE431' and 346-347 'The DE431-vs-DE440 hypothesis'. Auditor's a-b (Swiss .se1 vs Swiss on the DE440 JPL binary) Moon max 0.0104 arcsec reproduced from their swiss.json. I went further on attribution using only cached Horizons data (Moon source DE441), cancelling the common IAU76/80 frame residual by subtracting the Sun's residual at each instant: Swiss .se1 Moon vs Horizons DE441 Moon rms 0.0018 / max 0.0042 arcsec, alpha-on-DE440s Moon vs Horizons rms 0.0043 / max 0.0103 arcsec, correlation of (a-b) with the DE440 residual -0.865, and a-b is V-shaped in time (0.0104 at 1851, under 0.001 over 1933-2012, 0.0085 at 2148) - the signature of DE440/DE441 lunar divergence away from the LLR span. So the 0.0107 arcsec Moon residual is the DE440-vs-DE441 difference, now measured rather than asserted. What is wrong is the severity and framing: RESULTS.md itself hedges at lines 232-233 ('a hypothesis consistent with the data, not a proven attribution') and 346-347 ('unexplained... not tested'); the rest of the tree correctly records DE441 (docs/engine-validation/README.md:33-34, swiss-node-polar/README.md:18, src/lib/engine/fixtures/swiss-eight-cases-policy.json:44); and no owner-facing tree document claims a DE440-over-DE431 advantage (FOUR-CONFIGURATIONS.md:36 explicitly disclaims superiority). The refuted 'premise' comes from the audit brief, not from the tree. One wrong factual parenthetical in a hedged evidence record, 0.2 days to fix, nothing shipped or claimed depending on it, is a minor defect by the rules, not a major unsupported claim.
